prompt: Write merge sort by hand as a generic method with List<? extends T> and Comparator<? super T>, keeping the sort stable, plus a natural-ordering version bounded by Comparable. Complete GenericMergeSorter in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Merge sort splits the list in half, sorts each half recursively, and walks the two sorted halves together. Stability comes down to one comparison: when the two front elements tie you must take the LEFT one, so writing the test as "take from the right only when it is strictly smaller" gets it right by construction. The wildcards follow the producer-extends, consumer-super rule -- the input only produces T values so it is List<? extends T>, while the comparator only consumes them so it is Comparator<? super T>, which is why a Comparator<Object> can sort a list of Contestants.
hints: Copy the input into a new ArrayList first. That gives you the guarantee that the caller's list is untouched, and lists of size 0 or 1 are then already sorted.
Merging is a two-index walk. Advance whichever side supplies the next element, then drain whatever is left over from the other side.
Stability hinges on ties: when the comparator returns 0, take from the LEFT half. Writing the condition as compare(right, left) < 0 makes that happen automatically.
